_comment: Single source of truth for the document tag vocabulary.
Read by scripts/migration/08f_ai_batch_refiner.py (to build the prompt) and by
Do not hardcode tag names anywhere else.
Orthogonality test for adding a tag: a tag is allowed to be concentrated in one
category as long as it SUBDIVIDES that category into groups a student would filter
on (e.g. 'Formularium' and 'Lesnotities' inside Samenvattingen). A tag that merely
RESTATES the category name (e.g. 'Slides' inside 'Slides / Lesmateriaal') carries no
information there - list it under redundant_in_category instead of deleting it, so it
keeps working in the categories where it is informative.
notes: 'Scan' is a MEDIUM: the document is an image or photo rather than selectable text. It says nothing about what is on the page - a photographed printed exam is a Scan.
'Handgeschreven' is CONTENT: the page carries handwriting. Apply it only when you can actually see handwriting, not merely because the document is a scan.
The two are independent and may appear together. Most scans in this archive are photographed printed material, so do not assume a scan is handwritten.
'MATLAB', 'Python', 'Java', 'C / C++', 'Excel' identify the programming language, software stack, or spreadsheet tool used.

divisions.prompt_hint: 'Deel 1', 'Deel 2', ... up to 'Deel 19' (only when the document is an explicitly numbered part)
